ety.text: Sanskritic formation from अन्ध (andh, “blind”) + भक्ति (bhakti, “devotion”); compare देशभक्ती (deśbhaktī, “patriot”).
Borrowed from Sanskrit अभिराम (abhirāma). By surface analysis, अभि- (abhi-) + राम (rām).
From Sanskrit अवहेलित (avahelita), past participle of अवहेला (avahelā) (neglect, disregard), from अव (ava) (down, away) + हेला (helā) (carelessness, negligence).

s.g: imam (one who leads the salat prayers in a mosque)

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian اِمَام (imām), borrowed from Arabic إِمَام (ʔimām).

Inherited from Proto-New Indo-Aryan *गप्प (gappa), probably onomatopoeic. Cognate with Persian گپ (gap), Punjabi ਗੱਪ (gappa) / گپّ (gappa), Bengali গপ (gop), Gujarati ગપ (gap), Nepali गफ (gaph), Odia ଗପ (gapa), Assamese গপ (gop).
Borrowed from Classical Persian جلاد (jallād), from Arabic جَلَّاد (jallād).
